summary: Add a durable browser job runner with two backends: the authenticated Safari bridge for owner-private pages and Cloudflare Browser Run for public pages. Represent each step as navigate/read/extract/click/type, persist evidence (URL, title, timestamp, selected text), retry transient failures, and expose a job result stream to the planner.
note: KEPT OPEN: the backend ROUTER now exists, the durable job runner still does not. Backend A ships: local-agent/browserSessions.js (chg-bc35ae04 / chg-2fffc681 / chg-086a6904). Backend B ships: cloud-relay/serverBrowser.js (chg-81e5c92d, implemented). ROUTER DONE 2026-08-07 — local-agent/originFanOut.js chooseBackend() is the selector this entry named: owner-private -> Safari (only it holds the sessions); public -> Browser Run (only it is awake when the Mac sleeps); LAN / private IP / localhost -> Safari only, decided by serverBrowser.normalizePublicUrl rather than a second copy of that logic; relay budget spent -> Safari; explicit backend:"safari"|"relay" always honoured. An owner-private page is deliberately NOT failed over to the relay when Safari is down: the relay cannot hold the session, so the trip buys a login wall at the price of one of ten daily browser-minutes, and reserving that budget is what keeps the public leg answerable. Free-tier limits are enforced rather than documented: relay lane is serial, paced to 1 action per 10s, and a UTC-day browser-ms tally persists in .pendant-relay-browser-budget.json (GET /origins/budget). MISSING STILL: no durable job runner — no jobId, no persistence across a restart, no retry of transient failures — and no job result stream to the planner. serverBrowser is still unreachable from the voice path (chg-f527c3bc, unapplied wiring diff).
